thread:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — dedicated-pool acmecorp-prod GPU exhaustion detected (severity: P1) :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: alerts: 6x gpu-util > 98% across all nodes in pool acmecorp-prod for 8m, pending queue growth. Notified on-call.

Emily Perez: I’m on it. Getting the current picture — queue length, running jobs, and whether autoscaler is blocked.

Sanjay Shah: Logs show sustained batch job from tenant acmecorp is pinning all GPUs. Prefetch batch workload started at 01:04 UTC. GPU mem 100% on 8 GPUs, OOM not yet.

Marta K: Is this a single-tenant dedicated pool?

Emily Perez: Yes — acmecorp-prod is their dedicated pool. No other tenants on these nodes.

Liam Chen: Dumping node/Pod state now.

Liam Chen: ```
# kubectl -n dedicated-acme get pods -o wide --show-labels
NAME                          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
batch-prep-0                  1/1     Running   0          2h   node-gpu-03
model-train-1                 1/1     Running   0          1h   node-gpu-01
model-train-2                 1/1     Running   0          1h   node-gpu-02
inference-service-0           1/1     Running   0          4d   node-gpu-04

# nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv
PID, Process name, Used GPU Memory
4231, python, 24576 MiB
4320, python, 24576 MiB
... (full dump attached)
```

Emily Perez: Queue backlog metric: acme.request_queue_depth spiked from 12 -> 420 in 10m. Latency SLOs breached for 15m on host customers.

acct-eng (Account Team): I'm looping in AcmeCorp support — they need realtime updates. They reported increased tail latency via their own monitors.

customer-support: Acme reported errors 503 for ~20% of requests starting ~01:10 UTC. They want mitigation ASAP.

Sanjay Shah: Two mitigation paths: 1) Evict/terminate non-critical batch jobs in pool, free GPUs. 2) Trigger burst to spare capacity (if account permissions allow). We should prefer non-disruptive first.

Marta K: Autoscaler health: scaling disabled for this pool due to reserved capacity config (customer opted for strict capacity). There is a burst override but it requires engineering approval + account team's sign-off due to billing.

Emily Perez: Who can toggle the burst override?

Liam Chen: Platform engineers can, but we need documented approval. We can do temporary ingress of 4 on-demand GPUs from shared pool (hot spare) — that would relieve latency in ~3m.

Sanjay Shah: Eviction plan: Identify pods with label 'workload=batch' and graceful terminate with 60s. That will drop chunked prefetch and free 2 GPUs per pod on these nodes. Risk: training checkpoints may be lost if job not configured with checkpointing.

Emily Perez: Cross-check checkpoint state now. If batch jobs are preemptible and have checkpoints, evict. Otherwise, burst.

Liam Chen: Checkpoint status: batch-prep-0 has last checkpoint at 00:50 UTC (OK), model-train-1 & 2: last checkpoint 00:55 UTC but model-train uses multi-GPU sync — evicting both could cause wasted epoch progress.

acct-eng (Account Team): AcmeCorp on phone. They approve temporary burst if it restores production latency and we notify about cost. They request we avoid killing training until we confirm checkpointing.

Emily Perez: Decision: enable burst override to add 4 on-demand GPUs + evict the batch-prep pod (non-critical) now. Notify Acme and monitor.

ops-bot: ACTION: burst_override enabled by Emily P. added 4 gpus from shared-pool to acmecorp-prod (request id: br-1967008888).

Emily Perez: Running eviction now: ```kubectl -n dedicated-acme delete pod batch-prep-0 --grace-period=60```

Liam Chen: batch-prep-0 terminated cleanly, GPUs freed. Node utilization down to 72% across pool. Queue depth dropping: 420 -> 110 in 4m.

Sanjay Shah: Burst join completed; new machines provisioned and inference pods autoscaled onto them. Tail latency returning to normal per dashboards.

customer-support: AcmeCorp confirms errors are falling; tail p95 latency back within SLO for key endpoints. They thanked us but asked for root cause and long-term plan.

Emily Perez: Marking incident as mitigated for customer-visible impact. Remaining steps: 1) keep burst active for 60m to drain backlog, 2) run postmortem to decide on reserved capacity bump or scheduling constraints, 3) follow up with account for contract change if they want burst auto-enabled.

Marta K: Follow-up items assigned to eng-platform and SRE: evaluate policy UX for customers who want auto-burst with billing consent. Also add a check that dedicated pools with "no autoscale" still allow emergency burst with documented approval path.

Sanjay Shah: Moving to post-incident analysis channel. We'll collect logs, pod histories, and checkpoint metadata.

Emily Perez: Handoff: @Sanjay will take the write-up; @Marta will do capacity policy changes; I'll continue customer communication until handoff to AM. Night on-call (Liam) — you're the primary for watch while burst is active.

Liam Chen: Acknowledged. Monitoring alerts set to elevated for next 2h.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigated -> customer impact resolved. Handed off to follow-up phase. Severity downgraded to P2.

Emily Perez: Thanks team. We'll create the timeline and initial RCA draft within 24h. :white_check_mark:

acct-eng (Account Team): I'll summarize the customer communication and propose contract options (reserved bump vs paid burst) in the follow-up ticket.

Sanjay Shah: Attachments: full nvidia-smi dumps, kube events, autoscaler logs (br-1967008888).

customer-support: Closing note from Acme: "Thanks — latency fixed and appreciate the transparent updates."

Emily Perez: Closing thread here; moving logs to incident tracker.
